items.title: QHEAppE Client
items.text:
QHEAppE Client is the Python client of QaaS (Quantum-as-a-Service), developed by IT4Innovations. It gives access to IQM quantum computers, such as the VLQ machine at IT4Innovations, through the LEXIS Platform and HEAppE.

You write circuits in Qiskit; the client handles LEXIS authentication, finds the quantum backends of your LEXIS project, transpiles circuits for the hardware, submits jobs through the HEAppE QScheduler API and returns the results as Qiskit objects.

The client is distributed in the qaas package and imported as qheappe_client.

items.title: Quick start
items.text:
Install the client with the IQM libraries (Python 3.12):

pip install 'qaas[iqm_qiskit]' --extra-index-url https://opencode.it4i.eu/api/v4/projects/107/packages/pypi/simple

Run a Bell-state circuit:

from qheappe_client import QProvider
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit

# Without a token, a browser login to LEXIS opens
provider = QProvider(lexis_project="YOUR_LEXIS_PROJECT")

backend = provider.get_backend(
    lexis_resource="YOUR_QUANTUM_RESOURCE", backend_name="VLQ"
)

qc = QuantumCircuit(2)
qc.h(0)
qc.cx(0, 1)
qc.measure_all()

job = backend.run(backend.transpile(qc), shots=1000)
counts = job.result(qiskit_legacy=True).get_counts()
print(counts)  # e.g. {'00': 497, '11': 489, '01': 8, '10': 6}

job.result() returns a Qiskit PrimitiveResult by default, or a legacy Result with qiskit_legacy=True. See PrimitiveResult vs. legacy Result for the difference.

items.title: API Reference
items.text:
This page covers the main classes of the QHEAppE Client. The full, generated reference of every module is in the API reference (pdoc).

from qheappe_client import QProvider, QBackendIQM, QJob, QBackendMetadata
from qheappe_client.utils import QException, QAuthException

items.title: QProvider
items.text:
Entry point. Authenticates to LEXIS and creates backends for the quantum resources of a LEXIS project. Clients are cached per resource.

provider = QProvider(lexis_project, token=None, lexis_api_url="https://api.lexis.tech/")
Parameter Type Description lexis_project str LEXIS project short name token str \| None LEXIS access token; if None, an interactive py4lexis login is started lexis_api_url str LEXIS API base URL

items.title: get_backend(lexis_resource, backend_name=None, calibration_set_id=None, *, use_metrics=False, strict_iqm_version=True) -> QBackendIQM
items.text:
Creates a backend for a quantum resource. Checks that the installed IQM libraries work with the backend's station-control version.

Parameter Type Default Description lexis_resource str \| QBackendMetadata — Quantum resource name, or metadata from available_backends() backend_name str \| None None Backend (cluster) name; required if the resource has several calibration_set_id UUID \| None None Calibration set; None = current default use_metrics bool False Load calibration metrics into the transpiler target strict_iqm_version bool True Raise QException on an IQM version mismatch; False only warns

items.title: available_backends(lexis_resource) -> dict[str, QBackendMetadata]
items.text: All backends of a resource, including unavailable ones (check .available and .error).

items.title: get_backend_info(lexis_resource, backend_name=None, calibration_set_id=None) -> QBackendMetadata
items.text: Metadata of one backend, including its architecture, without creating a backend.

items.title: get_client(lexis_resource, backend_name=None) -> QClient
items.text: Low-level client bound to a resource or backend (machine metrics, job info, sessions).

items.title: get_pulla(lexis_resource, backend_name=None, calibration_set_id=None, *, strict_iqm_version=True, walltime_limit_secs=3600, job_name="qpulla_job", use_sessions=False) -> QPulla
items.text:
Pulse-level access to a backend, see QPulla. Needs qaas[iqm_qiskit] (iqm-client 36) and QScheduler v0.2.2+ with pulse access enabled for the machine; raises NotImplementedError with another IQM stack.

Argument Default Description walltime_limit_secs 3600 HEAppE walltime limit of each pulse task job_name "qpulla_job" HEAppE job name use_sessions False Run tasks in QScheduler sessions

items.title: clear_cache()
items.text: Forget the cached clients; the next call connects again.

items.title: QBackendIQM
items.text: Qiskit BackendV2 for an IQM quantum computer. Returned by QProvider.get_backend().

items.title: architecture
items.text:
The backend's dynamic quantum architecture (from the active calibration set).

Attribute Description architecture.qubits Qubit names architecture.gates Supported gates and their loci architecture.calibration_set_id Calibration set the architecture belongs to

num_qubits and target are the standard Qiskit backend properties.

items.title: transpile(circuits, **kwargs) -> QuantumCircuit | list[QuantumCircuit]
items.text: Transpiles one circuit or a list of circuits to the native gate set and connectivity. Keyword arguments go to IQM's transpile_to_IQM (e.g. optimize_single_qubits, initial_layout, restrict_to_qubits).

items.title: run(run_input, shots, **options) -> QJob
items.text:
Submits one transpiled circuit or a list of them as one job.

Parameter Type Default Description run_input QuantumCircuit \| list[QuantumCircuit] — Transpiled circuit(s) shots int — Number of shots (required) job_name str "qiskit_qasm_job" Job name in HEAppE walltime_limit_secs int 3600 Walltime limit of the job circuit_compilation_options CircuitCompilationOptions IQM default IQM server-side compilation options

items.title: create_circuit_job_definition(run_input, shots=1024, ...) -> CircuitJobDefinition
items.text: Builds the IQM job definition without submitting it. create_run_request is an alias (iqm-client 35 name).

items.title: iqm_stack
items.text: Which IQM library generation the backend uses (IQMStack.IQM36 or IQMStack.IQM35).

items.title: client -> QPulla
items.text: IQM client of the backend, connected through HEAppE (created on first use, IQM 36 stack only). It lets IQM's helpers that take a backend work with this one, e.g. iqm.qiskit_iqm.pulse_level_utils.qiskit_to_iqm(backend, circuits).

items.title: QPulla
items.text:
Pulse-level access (IQM Pulla) to one backend. A subclass of iqm.iqm_client.IQMClient whose requests go through HEAppE/QScheduler, so IQM's pulse-level API works as IQM documents it. Returned by QProvider.get_pulla().

Member Description backend The QBackendIQM of the same machine qiskit_to_iqm(circuits) Transpiled Qiskit circuits → IQM circuits and a compiler with the backend's qubit mapping get_qiskit_compiler(...) Compiler that also transpiles Qiskit circuits get_standard_compiler(...) IQM's standard compiler (default calibration set) submit_playlist(run_definition, context=...) Submit a compiled RunDefinition; returns IQM's RunJobTracker sweep_job_to_qiskit(job, shots=...) Results of a finished job as a Qiskit Result get_calibration_set(), get_calibration_set_stash() Calibration data get_chip_label(), get_chip_topology() Chip information get_dynamic_quantum_architecture(), get_static_quantum_architecture() Architectures executor Submission options: walltime_limit_secs, job_name, use_sessions

The returned RunJobTracker works as in IQM's client: wait_for_completion(), status, cancel(), result(), result_sweep(). Its job_id is the HEAppE job id as a UUID (UUID(int=heappe_job_id)).

Writing calibration data (observations, runs, sequences) and get_health() are not available through HEAppE and raise NotImplementedError.

items.title: QJob
items.text: A submitted job. Returned by QBackendIQM.run(), or created from an existing HEAppE job ID with QJob(backend, job_id).

items.title: job_id
items.text: HEAppE job ID as an int. job.job_id() returns it as a string (Qiskit style).

items.title: result(with_measurements=None, key_order_left_to_right=False, qiskit_legacy=False) -> PrimitiveResult | Result
items.text:
Waits until the job finishes and returns the results.

Parameter Default Description with_measurements None Include per-shot results. None follows the memory option given to backend.run() (default False) key_order_left_to_right False Bit order of bitstrings; False = Qiskit's right-to-left order qiskit_legacy False Return a legacy Result instead of a PrimitiveResult

Accessing the results:

Result type Counts Per-shot results PrimitiveResult res[i].data.meas.get_counts() res[i].data.meas.get_bitstrings() Result (legacy) res.get_counts() res.get_memory()

Raises RuntimeError if the job failed or was cancelled.

items.title: status() -> JobStatus
items.text: Current job state as a Qiskit JobStatus.

items.title: QBackendMetadata
items.text:
Describes one backend of a quantum resource (returned by available_backends() and get_backend_info()).

Property Description backend_name Backend (cluster) name available / error Whether the backend can be used, and why not supplier, quantum_technology e.g. IQM, SUPERCONDUCTING qaas_version QScheduler version machine_info Parsed MachineInfo, incl. station_control_version dynamic_architecture / static_architecture IQM architectures, if loaded lexis_project, lexis_resource, heappe_url, allocated_units LEXIS and HEAppE details

items.title: Exceptions
Architecture
items.text:
The QHEAppE Client is the user-side part of the QaaS solution. It talks to two services:

  • LEXIS Platform — authentication, projects and quantum resources (which HEAppE instances and backends you may use)
  • HEAppE with QScheduler — the REST API in front of each quantum computer: machine information, calibration, job submission, results and job events
graph TD
    User["User code<br/>(Qiskit circuits)"]
    P["QProvider"]
    B["QBackendIQM / QJob"]
    F["QBackendIQMFactory<br/>(IQM version check)"]
    C["QClient"]
    LEXIS["LEXIS Platform<br/>(auth, projects, resources)"]
    HEAppE["HEAppE + QScheduler<br/>(REST API, job events)"]
    IQM["IQM quantum computer<br/>(station control)"]

    User --> P
    User --> B
    P --> F
    F --> B
    P --> C
    B --> C
    C --> LEXIS
    C --> HEAppE
    HEAppE --> IQM

items.title: QProvider
items.text: The entry point. Takes a LEXIS project and token, creates one QClient per quantum resource (cached), and builds backends through QBackendIQMFactory.

items.title: QClient
items.text:
Does all network communication, asynchronously (aiohttp), with a synchronous API on top. Sync calls run on the client's own background event loop, so they also work inside Jupyter and other code that already runs an event loop.

  • verifies the LEXIS token and checks access to the project and resource
  • discovers the HEAppE clusters (backends) of the resource and checks their availability
  • reads MachineInfo, the machine architecture and calibration data from QScheduler
  • submits jobs, fetches results and artifacts, cancels jobs, and manages QScheduler sessions
  • listens to the HEAppE job-event websocket to know when a job finishes

items.title: QBackendIQM and QJob
items.text: A Qiskit BackendV2 built from the backend's IQM dynamic architecture. It transpiles circuits with IQM's transpiler, serializes them into an IQM circuit job definition and submits it through QClient. QJob waits for the job and converts the results into a Qiskit PrimitiveResult or legacy Result.

items.title: QBackendIQMFactory (IQM version selection)
items.text:
Only one generation of the IQM client libraries can be installed at a time (iqm_qiskit = iqm-client 36, iqm35_qiskit = iqm-client 35). The factory compares the installed one with the station_control_version the backend reports in MachineInfo:

Backend station-control Works with 50.x (current) iqm-client 36 49.x (older) iqm-client 36 (recommended) or iqm-client 35 unknown the installed version, with a warning

On a mismatch it raises a QException with the pip install command for the right extra. The differences between the IQM versions are kept in small adapter modules (qheappe_client.iqm_compat.iqm35 / iqm36).

items.title: Job flow
items.text:
What happens when you call backend.run(...) and job.result():

  1. Job definition — the transpiled circuits are converted into an IQM circuit job definition (JSON), including the calibration set and shot count.
  2. Submission — QClient sends it to POST /heappe/QScheduler/CreateAndSubmitJob; HEAppE returns the job ID.
  3. Execution — QScheduler queues the job and runs it on the IQM quantum computer.
  4. Completion — QClient waits for a terminal job state from the HEAppE event websocket (/heappe/Events).
  5. Results — the results of each task are fetched from GET /heappe/QScheduler/GetTaskResult (and per-shot measurements as task artifacts) and converted into Qiskit result objects.

items.title: Design decisions
items.text:
• Client-side transpilation — circuits are transpiled against the backend's current calibration before submission, so the backend always receives native-gate circuits.
  • Current calibration — the dynamic architecture is loaded when the backend is created; calibration_set_id pins a specific one, and use_metrics=True adds calibration quality metrics to the transpiler target.
  • Direct QScheduler API — jobs are submitted through the QScheduler REST API instead of HEAppE command templates (used by the legacy qaas client).
  • Optional IQM dependencies — the IQM libraries come from extras, so the client can support more than one IQM release.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• Python 3.12 (>=3.12,<3.13)
  • A LEXIS Platform project with an allocated quantum resource (see Usage)

A virtual environment (venv or uv) is strongly recommended.

items.title: Install the QHEAppE Client
items.text:
The QHEAppE Client is published in the qaas package on the IT4Innovations package index. Install it together with one IQM extra:

pip install 'qaas[iqm_qiskit]' --extra-index-url https://opencode.it4i.eu/api/v4/projects/107/packages/pypi/simple

The --extra-index-url is required: it also provides py4lexis, which handles LEXIS authentication and is installed automatically.

To pin a version, put the extra before it:

pip install 'qaas[iqm_qiskit]==1.0.0' --extra-index-url https://opencode.it4i.eu/api/v4/projects/107/packages/pypi/simple

In a Jupyter notebook use %pip install ... with the same arguments and restart the kernel afterwards.

Install an IQM extra

pip install qaas alone does not install Qiskit or the IQM libraries. Importing qheappe_client without them raises an ImportError that prints the install command.

items.title: IQM extras and backend compatibility
items.text:
Install exactly one of the extras. They pin different, incompatible versions of the IQM libraries.

Extra IQM libraries Works with backends on station-control Use it when iqm_qiskit (alias iqm36_qiskit) iqm-client 36.x 50.x (current) and 49.x (older) Always, including Pulla (pulse-level access) — recommended iqm35_qiskit iqm-client 35.x 49.x only Only for the legacy qaas.client

When you call QProvider.get_backend(), the client reads the station-control version the backend reports and checks that the installed IQM libraries work with it. If they don't (for example iqm35_qiskit against a 50.x backend), you get a QException with the command for the right extra. Pass strict_iqm_version=False to get a warning instead.

items.title: Server versions
items.text:
Minimum versions on the server side:

Feature HEAppE QScheduler Circuit jobs 6.6+ 0.2+ Pulse-level access (Pulla) 6.7.0+ 0.2.2+, with pulse access enabled for the machine

Pulse-level access (Pulla)

QProvider.get_pulla() needs iqm_qiskit (iqm-client 36.x, iqm-pulla 15.x). With iqm35_qiskit it raises NotImplementedError.

items.title: Development install
items.text:
git clone https://github.com/It4innovations/quantum-as-a-service.git
cd quantum-as-a-service
pip install -e '.[iqm_qiskit,testenv]' --extra-index-url https://opencode.it4i.eu/api/v4/projects/107/packages/pypi/simple

testenv adds pytest, pytest-dotenv and pytest-timeout. Run the offline tests with:

python -m pytest tests/qheappe/test_unit.py tests/qheappe/test_iqm_compat.py

The live tests (tests/qheappe/test_integration.py) need a LEXIS token and project settings; see .env.test.example.

items.title: Main dependencies
items.text:
Package Version Purpose py4lexis 7.1.* LEXIS Platform authentication Py4HEAppE 3.1.* HEAppE API client aiohttp 3.14.* Async HTTP and job-event websocket PyJWT[crypto] 2.10.* LEXIS token verification qiskit >=2.0,<2.2 Circuits and results (from the IQM extra) iqm-client[qiskit] 36.0.* / 35.0.* IQM transpilation and job definitions (from the IQM extra)

The full list is in pyproject.toml.

items.title: Legacy qaas client
items.text: The repository also contains the previous client (qaas.client), which runs jobs through HEAppE command templates and is built on Pulla. It only works with qaas[iqm35_qiskit]. New code should use the QHEAppE Client (qheappe_client).

items.title: Usage
items.text:
You need a LEXIS Platform project with an allocated quantum resource (for example the VLQ machine at IT4Innovations, VSB – Technical University of Ostrava). How to get an allocation for VLQ is described in the IT4I documentation; access to LEXIS projects is described there and in the LEXIS Platform documentation.

You will need two names from your project:

  • LEXIS project — the project short name, e.g. EU-XX-XXX
  • Quantum resource — the name of the quantum resource in that project, e.g. VLQ-EU

Ask the PI of your LEXIS project if you don't know them.

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
QProvider needs a LEXIS access token. There are two ways to provide it:

from qheappe_client import QProvider

# 1. Interactive: without a token, a LEXIS login opens in the browser
provider = QProvider(lexis_project="YOUR_LEXIS_PROJECT")

# 2. Token: e.g. for scripts on remote machines or CI
import os

provider = QProvider(
    lexis_project="YOUR_LEXIS_PROJECT", token=os.environ["LEXIS_TOKEN"]
)

You can get a token once through an interactive py4lexis login:

from py4lexis.session import LexisSession

token = LexisSession().get_access_token()

The client verifies the token and checks that you have access to the project and resource. If not, it raises QAuthException with the projects or resources you do have access to.

items.title: Finding backends
items.text:
A quantum resource can have one or more backends (quantum machines behind HEAppE clusters):

backends = provider.available_backends("YOUR_QUANTUM_RESOURCE")
for name, md in backends.items():
    print(name, "available" if md.available else f"unavailable: {md.error}")

Detailed information about one backend:

info = provider.get_backend_info("YOUR_QUANTUM_RESOURCE", backend_name="VLQ")
print(info.supplier, info.quantum_technology)
print(
    "QScheduler:",
    info.qaas_version,
    "| station-control:",
    info.machine_info.station_control_version,
)

items.title: Connecting to a backend
items.text:
backend = provider.get_backend(
    lexis_resource="YOUR_QUANTUM_RESOURCE", backend_name="VLQ"
)

backend_name selects the backend (here the VLQ machine). You can leave it out if the resource has only one backend.

Useful options of get_backend():

Option Description backend_name Backend (cluster) to use; required if the resource has several calibration_set_id Use a specific calibration set (UUID) instead of the current default use_metrics Load calibration quality metrics into the transpiler target (better qubit selection) strict_iqm_version True (default): raise if the installed IQM libraries don't work with the backend; False: only warn

items.title: Inspecting the hardware
items.text:
print("Qubits:", backend.architecture.qubits)
print("Gates:", list(backend.architecture.gates))
print("Calibration set:", backend.architecture.calibration_set_id)
print("Number of qubits:", backend.num_qubits)

items.title: Transpiling circuits
items.text:
Circuits must be transpiled to the IQM native gate set and qubit connectivity before they are run:

from qiskit import QuantumCircuit

qc = QuantumCircuit(2)
qc.h(0)
qc.cx(0, 1)
qc.measure_all()

qc_transpiled = backend.transpile(qc)

transpile() also accepts a list of circuits. Keyword arguments are passed to IQM's transpile_to_IQM, for example optimize_single_qubits=False, initial_layout=... or restrict_to_qubits=[...].

items.title: Running a job
items.text:
job = backend.run(qc_transpiled, shots=1000, job_name="bell_state")
print("HEAppE job ID:", job.job_id)
  • shots is required.
  • Pass a list of transpiled circuits to run several circuits in one job.
  • job_name sets the name of the job in HEAppE.

items.title: Reading results
items.text:
job.result() waits until the job finishes. It returns a Qiskit PrimitiveResult by default, or a legacy Qiskit Result with qiskit_legacy=True:

# PrimitiveResult: one entry per circuit
result = job.result(with_measurements=True)
meas = result[0].data.meas
print(meas.get_counts())
print(meas.get_bitstrings()[:10])  # per-shot results

# Legacy Result
legacy = job.result(qiskit_legacy=True, with_measurements=True)
print(legacy.get_counts())
print(legacy.get_memory()[:10])  # per-shot results

items.title: PrimitiveResult vs. legacy Result
items.text:
Both contain the same measurement data; they differ in shape and in which Qiskit code expects them.

PrimitiveResult (default) Legacy Result (qiskit_legacy=True) Qiskit API Current Qiskit primitives format (as returned by SamplerV2) Older backend.run() format (qiskit.result.Result) Several circuits One entry per circuit: result[i] One experiment per circuit: result.get_counts(i) Counts result[i].data.meas.get_counts() result.get_counts() Per-shot results result[i].data.meas.get_bitstrings() result.get_memory() Use it for New code, Qiskit primitives-based workflows Existing code and tutorials that call get_counts() on the result

The measurements are always in the meas register of a PrimitiveResult.

Argument Default Description with_measurements None Include per-shot results (bitstrings / memory). None follows backend.run(..., memory=True); an explicit True/False always wins key_order_left_to_right False Bit order of the bitstrings; False matches Qiskit's right-to-left order qiskit_legacy False Return a legacy Result instead of a PrimitiveResult

items.title: Getting the results of an earlier job
items.text:
You can attach to a job submitted earlier using its HEAppE job ID:

from qheappe_client import QJob

job = QJob(backend, 12345)
counts = job.result(qiskit_legacy=True).get_counts()

items.title: Full example
items.text:
from qheappe_client import QProvider
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit

provider = QProvider(lexis_project="YOUR_LEXIS_PROJECT")
backend = provider.get_backend(
    lexis_resource="YOUR_QUANTUM_RESOURCE", backend_name="VLQ"
)

qc = QuantumCircuit(2)
qc.h(0)
qc.cx(0, 1)
qc.measure_all()

job = backend.run(backend.transpile(qc), shots=1000, job_name="bell_state")
counts = job.result(qiskit_legacy=True).get_counts()

for state, count in sorted(counts.items()):
    print(f"|{state}⟩: {count}")

items.title: Pulse-level access (Pulla)
items.text:
get_pulla() gives an IQM pulse-level client (QPulla, an iqm.iqm_client.IQMClient) for a backend. Compile circuits on your machine with IQM's compiler, then run the compiled job through HEAppE:

pulla = provider.get_pulla(lexis_resource="YOUR_QUANTUM_RESOURCE", backend_name="VLQ")

qc = QuantumCircuit(2)
qc.h(0)
qc.cx(0, 1)
qc.measure_all()

# Qiskit circuit -> IQM circuit + compiler for this backend
circuits, compiler = pulla.qiskit_to_iqm(pulla.backend.transpile(qc))

settings = compiler.get_settings(circuits=circuits)
settings.set_shots(1000)
run_definition, context = compiler.compile(circuits, settings=settings)

job = pulla.submit_playlist(run_definition, context=context)
job.wait_for_completion()
print(pulla.sweep_job_to_qiskit(job, shots=1000).get_counts())

Between get_settings() and compile() you can change pulse-level settings, or build schedules yourself with compiler.get_schedule_builder(); see IQM's Pulla documentation.

Example: examples/qheappe_client/pulse_level_custom_x_gate.ipynb defines a custom pulse shape for the prx gate, calibrates its amplitude with Rabi sweeps (Sweep over gate parameters), and compares X and X·X with the native gate. It follows the calibration workflow of Filippos Dakis, Experimental_results_IQM.

Requirements:

  • qaas[iqm_qiskit] (iqm-client 36.x, iqm-pulla 15.x)
  • QScheduler v0.2.2 or newer, with pulse access enabled for the machine
  • HEAppE 6.7.0 or newer (forwards the task Kind, machine artifacts and whole calibration sets)

items.title: Error handling
items.text:
All client errors derive from QException:

from qheappe_client.utils import QAuthException, QException

try:
    backend = provider.get_backend(
        lexis_resource="YOUR_QUANTUM_RESOURCE", backend_name="VLQ"
    )
    result = backend.run(backend.transpile(qc), shots=1000).result()
except QAuthException as e:
    print("Authentication / access problem:", e)
except QException as e:
    print("QHEAppE Client error:", e)

Common causes:

  • Expired or invalid LEXIS token
  • Wrong LEXIS project or quantum resource name (the message lists the available ones)
  • Backend unavailable or under maintenance
  • Installed IQM libraries don't work with the backend (the message gives the pip install command)
  • Circuits not transpiled for the backend

items.title: Async API
items.text:
QProvider and the backends use a synchronous API that also works inside Jupyter. For async code, QClient offers the same operations as coroutines:

import asyncio
from qheappe_client.qclient import QClient


async def main():
    async with await QClient.create(
        TOKEN, "YOUR_LEXIS_PROJECT", "YOUR_QUANTUM_RESOURCE"
    ) as client:
        md = await client.get_backend(backend_name="VLQ")
        print(md.backend_name, md.available)
        metrics = await client.machine_metrics()


asyncio.run(main())
